([[Long Beach, California]]) | college = [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] (2021–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 30 | draft_team = [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] | career_start = 2022 | career_end = | years1 = {{nbay|2022|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team1 = [[Denver Nuggets]] | years2 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022–2023]] | team2 = →[[Grand Rapids Gold]] | years3 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team3 = [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] | highlights = * [[NBA champion]] ([[2023 NBA Finals|2023]]) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2021]]) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 Latvia]]|[[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Peyton Tyler Watson''' (born September 11, 2002{{cite web|title=Peyton Watson|website=fiba.basketball|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2021/player/Peyton-Watson|access-date=July 29, 2021}}) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). A [[McDonald's All-American]] in high school, he played one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. Watson was selected in the first round of the [[2022 NBA draft]] with the 30th overall pick. ==High school career== Watson attended [[Long Beach Polytechnic High School]] in [[Long Beach, California]], joining the [[varsity team]] as a freshman.{{cite web |last=Bien-Kahn |first=Joseph |title=Peyton Watson's Crash Course in Stardom |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2895284-peyton-watsons-crash-course-in-stardom |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=April 27, 2021 |date=June 11, 2020}} After coming off the bench earlier in his career,{{cite web |last=Morales |first=Robert |title=Long Beach Poly guard Peyton Watson helping young Jackrabbits grow |url=https://www.presstelegram.com/2019/12/30/morales-long-beach-poly-guard-peyton-watson-helping-young-jackrabbits-grow/ |website=[[Press-Telegram]] |access-date=April 27, 2021 |date=December 30, 2019}} he assumed a leading role in his junior season.{{cite web |last=Guardabascio |first=Mike |title=Next One Up: Peyton Watson, Long Beach Poly Basketball |url=https://www.the562.org/2019/07/09/next-one-up-peyton-watson-long-beach-poly-basketball/ |website=The 562 |access-date=April 27, 2021 |date=July 9, 2019}} He averaged 23.2 points and eight [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game,{{cite web |title=USA TODAY High School Sports Awards: Los Angeles boys basketball nominees |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/highschool/2020/04/22/usa-today-hs-sports-awards-los-angeles-boys-basketball-nominees/2998404001/ |website=[[USA Today]] |access-date=April 27, 2021 |date=April 22, 2020}} earning [[Moore League]] MVP honors.{{cite web |last=Morales |first=Robert |title=UCLA's tournament run brought joy to Long Beach Poly coach Shelton Diggs |url=https://www.presstelegram.com/2021/04/23/uclas-tournament-run-brought-joy-to-long-beach-poly-coach-shelton-diggs/ |website=[[Press-Telegram]] |access-date=April 28, 2021 |date=April 23, 2021}} He was named to the rosters for the [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]].{{cite web |last=Guardabascio |first=Mike |title=Long Beach Poly's Peyton Watson Named McDonald's All-American |url=https://www.the562.org/2021/02/24/long-beach-polys-peyton-watson-named-mcdonalds-all-american/ |website=The 562 |access-date=April 28, 2021 |date=February 24, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== Watson was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], one of the top [[small forward]]s and the highest-ranked player from California in the 2021 recruiting class.{{cite web |last=Bolch |first=Ben |title=Familiarity breeds content as top prospect Peyton Watson picks UCLA |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2020-07-27/peyton-watson-picks-ucla |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=April 27, 2021 |date=July 27, 2020}} On July 27, 2020, he committed to playing college basketball for [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] over offers from [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] and [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]].{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=July 27, 2020 |title=Top California prospect Peyton Watson commits to UCLA |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29549961 |access-date=April 27, 2021 |website=[[ESPN]]}} He was frank with the Bruins coaching staff that he intended to be a [[one-and-done player]], leaving for the NBA after one year in college.{{cite news |last=Davis |first=Seth |author-link=Seth Davis |date=June 24, 2022 |title=What Peyton Watson brings to the Denver Nuggets: 'The mystery man of the draft' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3374282/2022/06/23/peyton-watson-nba-draft-denver-nuggets/ | accessdate = September 17, 2021 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Peyton Watson.jpg|left|thumb|upright|Watson with [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] in 2021]] As a freshman at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] in [[2021–22 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2021–22]], Watson arrived out of shape, primarily due to his high school senior season being disrupted by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]]. He joined an experienced UCLA group that had advanced to the [[Final Four]] of the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] a year earlier. All five starters returned, and he received no guarantees about his playing time.{{cite news|first=Mike|last=DeCourcy|title=Top freshman Peyton Watson takes shot at helping UCLA skip First Four and head straight toward Final Four|date=November 23, 2021|work=Sporting News|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/peyton-watson-freshman-ucla-final-four/1tn3o4v6q0skc12ose61hp9nlm|access-date=March 9, 2022}} Watson's defense was more advanced than his offense. However, the Bruins had other established scorers.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Making defense seem elementary, Peyton Watson quickly becomes a UCLA star|date=February 2, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-02-02/making-defense-seem-elementary-peyton-watson-becomes-ucla-basketball-star|access-date=March 1, 2022}} He received honorable mention for the [[Pac-12]] All-Freshman Team.{{cite news|first=Trevor|last=Allen|title=Utah Basketball Standouts Carlson, Stefanovic Receive All-Pac-12 Honors|date=March 8, 2022|website=KSLSports.com|url=https://kslsports.com/481664/utah-basketball-standouts-carlson-stefanovic-receive-all-pac-12-honors/|access-date=March 9, 2022}} He averaged 3.3 points and 2.9 rebounds in 12.6 minutes per game, and made just 32.2% of his [[field goal (basketball)|field goals]] and 22.6% of his [[three-pointers]]. His playing time was sporadic, and he logged 10 minutes or more in just two out of the last seven games of the season.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Peyton Watson announces he's leaving UCLA after one season, entering NBA draft|date=April 12, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-04-12/peyton-watson-announces-leaving-ucla-entering-nba-draft|access-date=April 15, 2022}} After the season, Watson [[Eligibility for the NBA draft|declared for the NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web|title= UCLA Men's Basketball G/F Peyton Watson Declares For 2022 NBA Draft, To Hire Agent|url=https://www.si.com/college/ucla/mens-basketball/ucla-mens-basketball-freshman-peyton-watson-declares-for-2022-nba-draft-to-hire-agent|first=Benjamin|last=Royer|date=April 12, 2022|access-date=April 12, 2022}} {{clear left}} ==Professional career== ===Denver Nuggets (2022–2026)=== Watson was selected by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in first round of the [[2022 NBA draft]] with the 30th overall pick.{{cite news|first=Adam|last=Grosbard|title=NBA Draft: UCLA's Peyton Watson to Nuggets, USC's Isaiah Mobley to Cavs|date=June 23, 2022|work=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2022/06/23/nba-draft-uclas-peyton-watson-goes-to-nuggets-in-first-round/|access-date=June 24, 2022}} He was then traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] along with two future second-round picks for [[JaMychal Green]] and a 2027 protected first-round draft pick.{{cite web|first=Ron|last=Gutterman|title=Nuggets Acquire Peyton Watson In Trade With Thunder|date=June 23, 2022|website=NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-peyton-watson-in-trade-with-thunder|access-date=June 24, 2022}} Possessing a wide wingspan, Watson was projected as a long-term project and expected to spend time developing with the [[Grand Rapids Gold]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite news|first=Mike|last=Singer|title=Nuggets rookie Peyton Watson flashes vast potential at Summer League showcase|date=July 25, 2022|work=The Denver Post|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2022/07/10/nuggets-rookie-peyton-watson-flashes-vast-potential-at-summer-league-showcase/|access-date=October 18, 2022}} He made 23 appearances (including two starts) for Denver during his rookie campaign, averaging 3.3 points, 1.6 rebounds, and 0.5 assists.{{Cite web|title=Peyton Watson 2022-23 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4576087/type/nba/year/2023|access-date=June 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Watson ended his rookie season as an [[NBA champion]] when the Nuggets defeated the [[2022–23 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]] in the [[2023 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]]. Watson played in 80 games (including four starts) for Denver in the [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24 season]], recording averages of 6.7 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 1.1 assists. He made 68 appearances (including 18 starts) for Denver during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 8.1 points, 3.4 rebounds, and 1.4 assists.{{Cite web|title=Peyton Watson 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4576087/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=June 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On November 19, 2025, Watson set new career-highs with 32 points and 12 rebounds in his third start of the season - a 125-118 road win over the [[2025–26 New Orleans Pelicans season|New Orleans Pelicans]].{{Cite web |last=Struck |first=Logan |date=2025-11-19 |title=3 Takeaways From Nuggets' Shorthanded Win Over Pelicans |url=https://www.si.com/nba/nuggets/onsi/news/3-takeaways-from-nuggets-shorthanded-win-over-pelicans |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20260121041117/https://www.si.com/nba/nuggets/onsi/news/3-takeaways-from-nuggets-shorthanded-win-over-pelicans|archive-date=January 21, 2026|access-date=2025-11-19 |website=Sports Illustrated}} His playing time continued to trend upward from mid-November while peaking at 44 minutes in a January overtime win over the 76ers. Watson won his first [[NBA Player of the Month and Week|NBA Western Conference Player of the Week Award]] for his play during the week of January 5-11, 2026, averaging 24.5 points, 8 rebounds, 4 assists, 1.3 steals, and 1.8 blocks.{{Cite web|title=PEYTON WATSON NAMED NBA WESTERN CONFERENCE PLAYER OF THE WEEK|date=January 12, 2026|website=nba.com|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/peyton-watsonnamed-nba-western-conference-playeroftheweek|access-date=January 20, 2026}} On January 22, Watson notched a new career-high in points, pouring in 35 points to help Denver defeat the [[2025–26 Washington Wizards season|Washington Wizards]], 107–97.{{Cite web|title=Peyton Watson scores career-high 35 points as short-handed Nuggets outlast Wizards 107-97|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/peyton-watson-scores-career-high-35-points-as-short-handed-nuggets-outlast-wizards-107-97/|access-date=March 6, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} His expansion in role and usage rate (an unforeseen 20.6%) coincided with injuries to core starters [[Aaron Gordon]] and [[Christian Braun]], who missed a combined 84 games missed throughout the year.{{cite web |title=Peyton Watson isn’t a Project anymore for Denver Nuggets |url=https://milehighsports.com/peyton-watson-isnt-a-project-anymore-for-denver-nuggets-klutch-sports-free-agency/ |website=Mile High Sports |last=Blackburn |first=Ryan |date=November 26, 2025 |access-date=July 24, 2026}}{{cite web |title=How Nuggets are navigating injuries to keep cooking on offense with Peyton Watson, Spencer Jones starting |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2025/12/14/nuggets-starting-lineup-offense-nikola-jokic-spencer-jones-two-way/ |website=The Denver Post |last=Durando |first=Bennett |date=December 14, 2025 |access-date=July 24, 2026}} While superstar [[Nikola Jokić]] was out of action for 15 games from the end of December to the end of January, Watson shined while averaging 22.1 ppg on 16.2 FGA and shooting 44% from distance.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/watsope01/gamelog/2026 |title=Peyton Watson 2025-26 Game Log |website=Basketball Reference |access-date=July 25, 2026}}{{cite web |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2026/01/24/nuggets-record-nikola-jokic-out-injury-jamal-murray-stats/ |title=5 trends that have defined Nuggets’ month without Nikola Jokic |website=The Denver Post |last=Durando |first=Bennett |date=January 24, 2026 |access-date=July 24, 2026}}{{cite web |title=Nuggets’ Peyton Watson emerging as breakout star with Nikola Jokic, other starters out |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2026/01/14/peyton-watson-stats-nuggets-lineup-nba-free-agents-2026/ |website=The Denver Post |last=Durando |first=Bennett |date=January 14, 2026 |access-date=July 24, 2026}} He made 54 total appearances, including 40 starts, for the Nuggets during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], averaging career highs of 14.6 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists, and 0.9 steals.{{cite news|first=Shams|last=Charania|title=Peyton Watson to Cavs, Max Strus to Clippers in multiteam trade|date=August 19, 2026|work=ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49664656/peyton-watson-cavaliers-max-strus-clippers-part-multi-team-trade-nuggets|access-date=August 19, 2026}}{{Cite web|title=Peyton Watson 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4576087/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=June 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} He scored 30+ points in a game four times, after none in his first three seasons. Peyton Watson did not play in the [[2026 NBA playoffs]] because his agent, Rich Paul, decided to keep him out to protect his health ahead of free agency.According to what Paul explained on the Game Over podcast, this decision aimed to take care of the player's future. This caused great frustration and annoyance among his Denver Nuggets teammates due to his inactivity.{{Cite web|title=Rich Paul Says Peyton Watson Was Held Out In Playoffs To Protect Him For Free Agency|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/287077/Rich-Paul-Says-Peyton-Watson-Was-Held-Out-In-Playoffs-To-Protect-Him-For-Free-Agency|access-date=August 24, 2026|website=realgm.com|language=en}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2026–present)=== On August 20, 2026, Watson was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] as part of a sign-and-trade deal. He signed a four-year, $88 million contract with the Cavaliers.{{Cite web|title=Cavaliers Acquire Peyton Watson |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-peyton-watson-260821|access-date=August 21, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Peyton Watson to Cavs, Max Strus to Clippers in multiteam trade |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49664656/peyton-watson-cavaliers-max-strus-clippers-part-multi-team-trade-nuggets |access-date=August 25, 2026 |website=ESPN}} ==National team career== Watson represented the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in Latvia. He averaged four points, 3.4 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game, helping his team win the gold medal.{{cite web |title=Peyton Watson (USA)'s profile – FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup 2021 |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2021/player/Peyton-Watson |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=July 12, 2021}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend|champion=y}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;
